info.title: Pingo Notify API | v3.0.0
info.description:
The v3 API is organized around **workspaces**. Every request runs against exactly one workspace, and your API token belongs to one.

Authenticate by sending your token in the `apikey` header. Target a different workspace you belong to with the `X-Account-Id` header.

The handshake Meta calls when you register the callback URL. Echoes `hub.challenge` back as `text/plain` when `hub.verify_token` matches the connection.

**No authentication** — Pingo registers this URL with Meta for you when you create an official connection.

post.description:
Where Meta posts inbound messages and status updates for an official connection.

Authenticity is verified with the `x-hub-signature-256` header (HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, keyed by your Meta app secret) whenever the connection has an app secret stored. Every failure — unknown connection, wrong type, bad signature — returns **404**, so connections cannot be enumerated.

post.description:
Creating a `WHATSAPP_UNOFFICIAL` connection with `qrcode: true` returns the first QR code inline — scan it to pair.

Creating a `WHATSAPP_OFFICIAL` connection requires your Meta credentials. Pingo validates them against the Graph API, then registers the inbound webhook for you. If webhook registration fails the whole creation is rolled back, so you never end up with a connection that silently receives nothing.

Counts against your plan connection limit. Official connections require a paid plan.

post.summary: Send a text or media message
post.description:
One endpoint covers text, image, video, audio and document. The message shape is decided by `mediaData`:

- **absent** → a text message, `text` is the body.
- **present** → a media message, and `text` becomes the **caption**.

`text` is required either way. For media with no caption, send `"text": ""`.

Inside `mediaData`, the `media` field takes **either a public URL or a base64 payload** — pick whichever you already have.

Each send consumes one message credit from your plan.

to.description: The recipient phone number, with country code.

text.description: The message body — or the media caption when `mediaData` is set. Required; send `""` for media with no caption.

linkPreview.description: Render the preview card for the first link in `text`. Set `false` to suppress it.

mentionsEveryOne.description: Group chats only — mentions every participant.

inputMode.description: `html` converts basic HTML to WhatsApp markup before sending.

value.text:
*Order confirmed*

Your package is _on the way_ and arrives tomorrow.

html.description:
Set `inputMode: "html"` and the API converts ``, ``, ``, `

` and `
` into WhatsApp markup. Handy when the copy comes out of a rich-text editor. Every other tag is stripped.

placeholders.description: `text` is a Handlebars template. The `{{money}}` helper formats a number as currency using `language` + `currency` — without them it falls back to `en-US`/`USD`.

value.text: Hi {{name}}! Your order totals {{money total}} and ships on {{date}}.

image.description: `text` is rendered as the caption below the image.

imageNoCaption.description: `text` is required by the schema, so send an empty string to get a bare image.

video.description: Use `video/mp4` — it is the format WhatsApp plays inline on every client.

value.text: A 30-second walkthrough of your new dashboard.

audio.description: This arrives as a playable **audio attachment**. For a push-to-talk voice note — the round bubble with a waveform — use `POST /send-voice-audio` instead.

document.description: `fileName` is what the recipient sees and what the file is saved as — always set it to something meaningful.

base64.description: When the file lives on your side and has no public URL, put the base64 payload straight into `media`. Mind the 10 MiB request-body ceiling — base64 inflates a file by roughly a third.

linkNoPreview.description: WhatsApp expands the first link by default. `linkPreview: false` keeps the message a plain line of text. `delay` holds the send for the given number of milliseconds.

post.description: WhatsApp expects a **WebP** sticker, 512×512, with a transparent background. Consumes one message credit.

sticker.description: A public URL or base64 payload.

base64.description: Same field, base64 payload instead of a link.

post.description:
Sends a **push-to-talk voice note** — the round bubble with a waveform, the one WhatsApp plays at 1×/1.5×/2×. This is not the same as an audio *file*: to send a playable attachment instead, use `mediaData` with `mediatype: "audio"` on `POST /chats/messages`.

The recipient sees a voice note only if the audio is in a format WhatsApp accepts for PTT (OGG/Opus). Send `encoding: true` and the provider transcodes for you — the safe default when the file is an MP3, an M4A, or anything a browser recorded.

Consumes one message credit.

audio.description: A public URL or base64 payload.

encoding.description: Ask the provider to transcode the audio into the format WhatsApp expects for voice notes.

transcoded.description: `encoding: true` converts the file so it lands as a real voice note instead of a broken attachment.

base64.description: For audio recorded in the browser and never uploaded anywhere.

post.description:
The only way to open a conversation on an official connection outside the 24-hour service window. The template must already be approved by Meta — list your approved templates with `GET /v3/connections/{id}/templates`.

The body follows Meta's own `components` format. Which components you must send is dictated by the template you built:

- A **body with variables** needs a `body` component whose `parameters` fill them, in order (`{{1}}`, `{{2}}`…) or by name (`parameter_name`, for NAMED templates).
- A **media header** needs a `header` component carrying an `image`, `video` or `document` parameter. Omit it and Meta rejects the send.
- A **dynamic URL button** needs a `button` component with `sub_type: "url"` and the `index` of that button.

A template with no variables takes no `components` at all.

noVariables.description: Fixed copy, nothing to fill in. Just the name and the language.

positional.description: Parameters are matched **by order**. The first one fills `{{1}}`, the second `{{2}}`, and so on.

named.description: When the template was built with NAMED parameters, each one carries a `parameter_name` and the order stops mattering.

imageHeader.description: A template whose header is an image. `link` must be a public URL Meta can fetch; alternatively upload the file first and pass `id`.

documentHeader.description: Same idea, with a PDF. `filename` is what the recipient sees.

currencyAndDate.description: Meta formats these on the device, in the recipient's locale. `amount_1000` is the amount times 1000 — R$149,90 becomes `149900`. `fallback_value` is shown when the locale cannot be formatted.

urlButton.description: The template defines the URL prefix; the parameter supplies the suffix. `index` is the button's position, counting from 0.

quickReply.description: The `payload` is what comes back to your webhook when the contact taps the button.

post.description:
A tappable menu: the contact opens `buttonText` and picks one row. Which row they chose comes back to you as the `rowId` of that row.

**Unofficial connections only.**

buttonText.description: The label of the button that opens the list.

rowId.description: Your own id for this row — it is what identifies the choice when the contact picks it.

menu.description: Sections group the rows visually. Every row needs a `rowId` you can recognize later.

value.title: Support
value.description: How can we help you today?
value.footerText: Reply anytime to talk to a human

post.description:
Up to a handful of tappable buttons under a message. Each button is discriminated by its `type`, and each type carries its own extra field:

| `type` | Extra field | What the tap does |
|---|---|---|
| `reply` | — | Sends `displayText` back as an ordinary reply |
| `url` | `url` | Opens the link |
| `call` | `phoneNumber` | Dials the number |
| `copy` | `copyCode` | Copies the code to the clipboard |
| `pix` | `currency`, `name`, `keyType`, `key` | Opens a Pix payment |

**Unofficial connections only.**

id.description: Your own id for this button — it identifies the tap.

name.description: Required when `type` is `pix`. The name of the payee.

key.description: Required when `type` is `pix`. The Pix key itself.

quoted.description: Reply to an earlier message. `key.id` is the `wamid` of the message being quoted.

reply.description: The classic yes/no. The tap comes back to you carrying the button `id`.

copy.description: One tap puts `copyCode` on the clipboard — good for coupons and one-time codes.

pix.description: Opens the payment right in the WhatsApp client, pre-filled with your Pix key.

mixed.description: Types can be combined freely in a single `buttons` array.

value.title: Your order is ready
value.description: Pick it up today, or have it delivered.

403.description: Reading messages requires Owner or Admin.

get.description:
Every media message delivered to your webhook carries a ready-to-use `downloadMediaUrl` pointing here. The signed `token` **is** the authentication — no `apikey` is needed, which is what lets your webhook consumer fetch the bytes directly.

The link is valid for **7 days** and returns the raw media bytes.

parameters.name: mediaId
parameters.description: The opaque media descriptor from the webhook payload.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The signed token from the webhook payload.

get.description: Read live from Meta, in every status (`APPROVED`, `PENDING`, `REJECTED`…). Official connections only.

post.description:
Submits the template to Meta for review — it comes back `PENDING`.

For a media header, upload the sample first with `POST /v3/connections/{id}/templates/header-media` and put the returned handle in `components[HEADER].example.header_handle`.

allowCategoryChange.description: Let Meta re-categorize instead of rejecting.

parameterFormat.description: `POSITIONAL` uses `{{1}}`; `NAMED` uses `{{name}}`. Meta assumes POSITIONAL when omitted.

201.description: The template, as Meta accepted it.

400.description: Meta rejected the template. The message carries Meta's own reason.

post.description: Uploads the sample image, video or document Meta reviews for a media header. Returns a `handle` to embed in the template as `components[HEADER].example.header_handle`. Max 16 MiB.

Note this is a **POST**, matching Meta's own API.

`name` and `language` are **immutable** — Meta locks them at creation, and they are ignored here. Editing sends the template back to `PENDING` review, and Meta refuses edits on approved templates outside its own quota rules.

400.description: Meta refused the edit. The message carries Meta's own reason.

delete.description: Deletes **one language variant**. Pingo resolves the template name for you when `name` is omitted, so the other languages of the same template survive.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The template name. Resolved automatically when omitted.

post.description:
Returns a short-lived token (**15 minutes, single use**) that you hand to the browser extension. Nothing is created yet — no connection, no provider instance.

Counts against your plan connection limit.

Called **by the browser extension**, not by your server. Authentication is the sync token from the previous step, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` — no `apikey`.

The token is single-use: replaying it returns 400.

session.description: The WhatsApp Web session harvested by the browser extension.

400.description: The session is missing, invalid, or the token was already used.

post.description: For a connection whose `mode` is `WA_SYNC` and whose session dropped. Does not consume a new connection slot.

400.description: The connection was not created with WhatsApp Sync.

post.description: Called by the browser extension with the reconnect token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

session.description: The WhatsApp Web session harvested by the browser extension.

400.description: The session is missing or invalid.

post.description:
Sends free-form text (optionally with one media attachment) from a `WHATSAPP_UNOFFICIAL` connection.

The whole audience travels in the request — there is no CSV upload, no saved segment, and **no scheduling**: the campaign starts sending immediately.

Each recipient gets `text` rendered with their own `variables` via `{{handlebars}}` placeholders. When `mediaData` is present the rendered text becomes the media **caption**.

Message credits for the full audience are reserved up front, atomically. If your plan cannot cover every recipient, nothing is created.

throttleMs.description: Milliseconds between sends. The default of 3 seconds paces an unofficial connection to roughly one message every 3 seconds, which is what keeps it from being flagged.

to.description: The phone number, with country code. Non-digits are stripped.

variables.description: Values bound into the `{{placeholders}}` in `text`, for this recipient only.

text.description: The same message for the whole audience — no variables, nothing to personalize.

value.name: Black Friday teaser
value.text: Our Black Friday starts tomorrow at 8am. Be ready 🔥

personalized.description: `text` is a Handlebars template and each target brings its own `variables`. A variable a target does not define simply renders empty.

value.name: Coupons — August
value.text: Hi {{name}}! Your coupon is *{{coupon}}* and it is worth {{money value}}.

media.description: With `mediaData` present, the rendered `text` becomes the media caption. One attachment per campaign.

value.name: August catalog
value.text: Hi {{name}}, the new catalog is out!

document.description: Any `mediatype` the single-message endpoint accepts works here too — `image`, `video`, `audio` or `document`.

value.name: Price list Q3
value.text: Our updated price list is attached.

400.description: Validation failed, no valid recipients survived normalization, or the connection is official.

post.description:
Sends an approved Meta template from a `WHATSAPP_OFFICIAL` connection. A template is mandatory here — outside the 24-hour service window Meta accepts nothing else.

Per-recipient `components` **fully replace** the campaign-level `template.components` for that recipient — they are not merged field by field.

Requires a paid plan.

throttleMs.description: Milliseconds between sends. The default of 3 seconds paces an unofficial connection to roughly one message every 3 seconds, which is what keeps it from being flagged.

components.description: Overrides the campaign template components for this recipient.

sameForEveryone.summary: One template, same values for everyone
sameForEveryone.description: The campaign-level `template.components` are used for every recipient.

perRecipient.description: Each target carries its own `components`, which **replace** the campaign-level ones wholesale for that recipient — they are not merged field by field, so repeat everything that recipient needs.

mediaHeader.description: The header image is part of the template payload, exactly as in a single send.

400.description: Validation failed, or the connection is not official.

403.description: Insufficient permissions, message quota exhausted, or a free plan.

get.description: Poll this to follow a campaign. The lifecycle is `QUEUED` → `RUNNING` → `COMPLETED`, with `CANCELED` and `FAILED` as off-ramps.

post.description:
Stops the campaign and refunds the message credits reserved for recipients that were never sent.

Idempotent: cancelling an already-finished campaign is a no-op that echoes back its existing terminal status with `refunded: 0`.

200.description: The campaign status and the credits refunded.

refunded.description: Message credits returned to your plan.

get.description: Agents only ever see conversations in inboxes they are a member of. Managers and above see the whole workspace.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: Items per page. Note the snake_case name — `perPage` is ignored.

parameters.name: assigneeTab
parameters.description: `me` shows conversations assigned to you, `unassigned` shows ownerless ones.

parameters.name: labels
parameters.description: Label ids — comma-separated or repeated. Matches ANY.

post.description:
Starts an outbound conversation with a contact and sends the first message in one call. Accepts `multipart/form-data` for attachments.

This is **find-or-create**: if an open conversation with that contact already exists in the inbox, it is reused rather than duplicated.

On a WhatsApp **official** inbox the 24-hour window is by definition closed for a brand-new conversation, so a `template` is required — anything else returns **422**.

The first message cannot be a private note.

422.description: The 24-hour WhatsApp service window is closed. Send an approved template instead.

example.message: Outbound window expired — channel requires a pre-approved template

get.description: The counts behind the inbox tabs. Accepts the same filters as the list endpoint.

patch.description: Status and assignee are **not** changed here — they have dedicated endpoints. Send `priority: null` to clear the priority.

post.description:
Valid transitions: `OPEN` → `RESOLVED`/`PENDING`/`SNOOZED`; `PENDING` → `OPEN`/`RESOLVED`; `SNOOZED` → `OPEN`/`RESOLVED`; `RESOLVED` → `OPEN`. Anything else returns 400.

Snoozing without `snoozedUntil` means "until the contact replies". A contact reply reopens a snoozed **or** resolved conversation automatically.

snoozedUntil.description: Only meaningful with `SNOOZED`. Omit to snooze until the contact replies.

400.description: Invalid status transition.

post.description:
Send `null` to explicitly un-assign; omit a field to leave it unchanged. At least one of the three is required.

Assigning a **bot** clears the human assignee, and assigning a **human** detaches the bot — a conversation has one owner.
Additive. Returns every label now on the conversation.
Resets `unreadCount` for the assignee.

get.description:
Cursor-paginated, **oldest first**, and it returns a bare array — not a pagination envelope. You have reached the start of history when you get back fewer than `limit` messages.

Pass the id of the oldest message you already hold as `cursor` to walk backwards.

Deleted messages are still returned, as tombstones with `deletedAt` set.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The id of the oldest message you already have.

post.description:
Accepts `application/json` (with base64 `attachments`) or `multipart/form-data` (file fields named `attachments`, `attachments[]` or `files`). Up to 10 files, 20 MiB each.

The message is created immediately with `status: PENDING` and delivered asynchronously — watch `helpdesk.message.status_changed` over the websocket, or poll the message.

**The 24-hour window:** on a WhatsApp official inbox, if the contact has not written in the last 24 hours you must send a `template` — anything else returns **422**. Private notes and templates skip the check.

Audio must be sent alone. A template accepts at most one attachment (its media header).

private.description: Make it a private note: visible to your team, never delivered to the contact, and never subject to the 24-hour window. Mention teammates with `(mention://user/<uuid>/Name)`.

template.description: An approved Meta template. Its presence marks the message as `TEMPLATE` and bypasses the 24-hour window.

dataUrl.description: A base64 **data URI** — `data:<mime>;base64,<payload>`. A bare base64 string is rejected. For files larger than the 10 MiB JSON body limit, use `multipart/form-data` instead.

localSourceId.description: Your own correlation id, echoed back in the response and over the websocket.

ptt.description: Mark the audio attachment as a voice note.

audioPeaks.description: The waveform of a voice note — up to 2000 samples, each between 0 and 1. Purely cosmetic: it is what your own UI draws in the bubble.

text.description: The everyday case: an agent answering the contact.

value.content: Hi Ana! Your order ships today and arrives on Thursday.

privateNote.description: Never delivered to the contact — only your team sees it. It is not a separate message type: it is an ordinary outgoing message with `private: true`. Mention a teammate with `(mention://user/<uuid>/Name)` and they get notified.

value.content: Customer already asked for a refund last month — (mention://user/0195f3b1-2c3d-7e4f-8a9b-0c1d2e3f4a5b/Bruno) can you take a look?

reply.description: `inReplyToId` is the id of the message being quoted — the contact sees it as a WhatsApp reply.

value.content: Yes, that is the correct address.

image.description: Inline attachments travel as base64 **data URIs**. `content` rides along as the caption.

document.description: Same mechanism, any MIME type. Up to 10 files per message, 20 MiB each — but anything past the 10 MiB JSON body limit has to go through `multipart/form-data`.

voiceNote.description: An audio attachment with `ptt: true` renders as a voice note. `audioPeaks` and `audioDurationSec` are what your interface draws in the bubble — they never reach the contact. Audio must be sent on its own: no other attachment alongside it.

template.description: When the contact has not written in over 24 hours, a plain message returns **422** on an official WhatsApp inbox. A `template` is the only thing Meta accepts — and it bypasses the window check entirely.

post.description:
The inbound half of the programmable `API` channel: this is how your own app delivers a customer message into the helpdesk.

Authenticate with **either** header:
- `x-helpdesk-token`: the inbox `inboundWebhookSecret`, verbatim. **Required for `multipart/form-data`.**
- `x-helpdesk-signature`: the hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw JSON body, keyed by that same secret.

The `event` field selects the operation and defaults to `message_created`. Use `status_update` to report delivery back, and `message_deleted` / `message_edited` to mirror changes.

A contact is resolved or created automatically from `sender`.

parameters.name: x-helpdesk-signature
parameters.description: Hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body.

sourceId.description: Your own id for the message. Used to correlate later status updates.

apiKey.name: apikey
apiKey.description:
Your API token, sent verbatim in the `apikey` header — including the `sk_live_` prefix.

Example: `apikey: sk_live_a1b2c3...`

Create and revoke tokens at `/v3/api-tokens`. The plaintext token is shown **only once**, at creation.

AccountId.name: X-Account-Id
AccountId.description:
The workspace (account) the request runs against.

Omit it and the request targets the account bound to your token. Send it to act on another workspace you are a member of — a workspace you do not belong to returns **403**.

message.description: A single message, or the list of validation failures.

acceptedAt.description: `null` while the invitation is still pending.

token.description: The plaintext token — returned **only** on creation and on a refresh. It is stored hashed and can never be read back.

messageGroupDelay.description: Seconds to buffer messages before delivering them as one batched array.

type.description: `WHATSAPP_UNOFFICIAL` pairs a real WhatsApp account (QR code or browser sync). `WHATSAPP_OFFICIAL` is the Meta Cloud API.

mode.description: How the connection was created — this is what decides the RECONNECT flow. `WA_QRCODE` asks for a new QR, `WA_OFFICIAL` re-registers the Meta webhook, `WA_SYNC` re-injects a browser session.

status.description: Live state reported by the provider.

base64.description: The QR rendered as a data URI image.

media.description: A public URL, or a base64 payload.

language.description: Accepts either a bare language code string (`"pt_BR"`) or the object form.

id.description: The Meta template id — required to edit or delete this variant.

body.description: The BODY text, hoisted for list previews.

totalTargets.description: The number of recipients actually queued, **after** normalization. This can be lower than the `targets` you sent — invalid and duplicate numbers are dropped silently, so always read this value back.

externalUrl.description: A signed, token-gated URL served by Pingo. It is **never** the provider CDN URL — media always egresses through us.

metadata.description: Carries `ptt`, `durationSec`, `peaks`, coordinates or vCard, depending on the type.

messageType.description: This **is** the direction. There is no separate direction field, and no `PRIVATE_NOTE` type — a private note is an `OUTGOING` message with `private: true`.

private.description: A private note — visible to agents, never delivered to the contact.

externalError.description: Why the provider rejected it, when `status` is `FAILED`.

deletedAt.description: Deleted messages stay in the timeline as tombstones.

identifier.description: External id — on WhatsApp this is the JID.

blocked.description: Inbound messages from a blocked contact are dropped before a conversation is even created.

displayId.description: The human-facing number, sequential per workspace.

status.description: `unsupported` is a normal terminal answer, not an error: the WhatsApp Cloud API cannot enumerate history or contacts.

enableAutoAssignment.description: Round-robin new conversations to online agents.

captureOutgoingEnabled.description: Mirror messages sent from the phone itself into the helpdesk.

query.description: An opaque payload — Pingo stores it verbatim and never interprets it.

responseDelaySeconds.description: `0` replies to every message. Anything higher waits that long and coalesces a burst of messages into **one** reply.

hasApiKey.description: The key itself is write-only and never returned.

onlyDuringBusinessHours.description: Measure the clock against the inbox working hours instead of wall-clock time.
